subject: Clustered self-serve credit grants flagged for NimbusCloud POC
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Suspicious cluster: self-serve credits granted to NimbusCloud-related signups

Team —

I pulled an automated alert this morning: between 2026-07-18T22:00 and 2026-07-19T03:00 UTC we issued self-serve trial credits to ~118 accounts that look related to the same signup cohort for a NimbusCloud evaluation. Quick signals:
- 74% of accounts used disposable/rotating email domains (e.g., nimbus-user-1729@mailinator.xyz, nimbuseval-*.emailtemp.org)
- 62 accounts have identical device fingerprint hashes (UA + canvas + timezone)
- High overlap in IP addresses across accounts (same /24 from a cloud provider)
- 56 accounts took the free credit within 2 minutes of signup (automation-like)

I've attached suspect_accounts.csv (summary) and a small extract of auth-logs.txt. My recommendation: pause automated credit issuance for the NimbusCloud POC cohort (pattern-matching the domain list in the CSV) until we triage.

Action items I suggest:
1) Pause self-serve grants for all signups that match the attached list and the disposable-domain regex.
2) Block further credits from the suspicious IP ranges for 24–48 hours.
3) Pull complete signup logs for the cohort and run anti-bot checks (captcha/behavior).
4) If Nimbus (the company) reaches out, route them to a manual verification path and offer a controlled, verified POC credit allotment.

I can run an expanded fingerprint correlation if we want to determine whether this is an internal test funnel or an external botnet.

- Dev
Senior Fraud Analyst
Redwood Inference

Hi John —

Ben looped me in — my team noticed a cluster of trial credits that matched "NimbusCloud" nomination data. We've temporarily paused automated credits for these signups while we verify a couple of details. Could you please: 

- Confirm the primary email domain(s) your evaluation team will use for the POC (e.g., @nimbuscloud.com)
- Provide a short list of employee names/emails who should receive immediate manual credits (PDF/Excel is fine)
- Share a company contact we can ring if we need to verify identity quickly (phone number or Slack)

If these signups are legitimate, we can fast-track manual credits for verified corporate emails and give you a 30-day POC extension. If we don't hear back within 48 hours we will continue the hold to protect the trial pool.

Thanks — appreciate the quick reply.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Suspicious cluster: self-serve credits granted to NimbusCloud-related signups — deeper signals

Following up after further correlation: the spike persists and several stronger bot signals show up when I stitch network + fingerprint data. Key points: 
- The majority of flagged accounts still originate from three cloud-provider /24s (same ASN).
- We see automated API-driven attempts that match common headless-browser fingerprints (canvas + WebGL entropy).
- The verified list John provided includes legitimate @nimbuscloud.com addresses but only ~18 of those map to activity in our suspect cohort.

Suggested approach:
1) Revoke automated credits for the accounts on suspect_accounts.csv that are not on John's verified list.
2) Issue manual credits (30k tokens equivalent) to the 18 verified corporate addresses John provided.
3) Keep the overall POC window at 30 days, but do not allow self-serve top-ups until we see normal human interaction (console logins + consistent IP ranges).
4) Notify legal if Nimbus requests an SLA/extended credit block — this will require an enterprise commitment.

I've attached ip-heatmap.png and a filtered auth-logs.txt that show the suspicious client fingerprints. If we want to be conservative we can also require a short video call for a few of the high-usage accounts.

Soojin Lee
Growth Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-20T15:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Clustered self-serve credit grants flagged for NimbusCloud POC — resolution

John —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and for the employee list. We've taken the conservative path:
- Automated self-serve credit issuance for the flagged cohort remains paused.
- We revoked credits on 94 accounts that matched the suspicious fingerprint/IP pattern and are rolling back any associated free-usage billing adjustments.
- We manually issued a 30,000-token POC credit to the 18 verified @nimbuscloud.com addresses you provided (you should see an email confirmation in a few minutes).
- We'll extend your POC window to 30 days from the manual issuance date, and we won't allow additional self-serve top-ups during that window unless we see validated console logins from the verified corporate addresses.

Marissa will coordinate the quick verification call if you want us to speed things up; Soojin and Dev will keep monitoring, and Ben (me) will be your single point of contact. If Nimbus decides to move to a committed Dedicated/Retail contract we can discuss an enterprise trial allocation and SLA.
